answer.rationale: The mandate needs the low-cost vendor's price, but a full primary switch with 14 days to a hard expiry (no auto-renew) and the line at 94% with zero buffer directly increases delivery risk, violating the primary objective. memory_c2 supports the low-cost vendor's economics, but onboarding was under calmer conditions; c3 shows a second source protects allocation, not cost. The highest-expected-value single move is to use the verified competitive quote as benchmarking leverage (c4: benchmarking moved the incumbent on both price and terms) to reopen the renewal before expiry, keeping integration stability (c1) as the no-line-down fallback. I want c4 verified because the entire negotiate path depends on whether benchmarking truly moved the incumbent, and the incumbent has already refused once this cycle. If negotiation fails inside the window, renew to protect the line and revisit the switch next cycle with buffer.
